title: Lid close action retries endlessly every 10 to 20 s when sleep or hibernate fails, draining the battery
line: When sleep or hibernate fails with the lid closed, Plasma no longer keeps retrying it every few seconds until the battery is empty.
explanation: After every resume, powerdevil checks again 10 s later and, if the lid is still closed, assumes an unintended wakeup and runs the lid action (sleep or hibernate) again. logind sends the same "resumed" signal (PrepareForSleep(false)) when a sleep attempt simply fails, so a failing hibernate was retried every 10-20 s for as long as the lid stayed closed, with no limit. The change records how long the system has spent suspended since boot (CLOCK_BOOTTIME minus CLOCK_MONOTONIC) when sleep starts and when it ends, and only re-triggers the lid action if that grew, i.e. the system really slept.

commits.message:
handlebuttonevents: don't retry the lid action when sleep failed

logind also reports a resume when a sleep attempt fails, so with the lid
closed a failing suspend or hibernate was retried every 10-20 s until
the battery ran out. Now it is only re-triggered after a real sleep.

BUG: 528651

media.caption: Master: lid closed for 100 s with every hibernate failing; powerdevil asks logind to hibernate 9 times, every 12 s
With the fix, same 100 s: one hibernate attempt; powerdevil sees the system did not sleep and does not retry

review.text: logind sending PrepareForSleep(false) after a failed sleep is systemd's behaviour, so detecting a real sleep in powerdevil is the right place. Comparing CLOCK_BOOTTIME minus CLOCK_MONOTONIC across the sleep is a simple, robust signal, and the re-trigger logic is unchanged after a real sleep. The fake logind and the clock shim cover failed sleeps, real sleeps and repeated lid closes. It no longer applies cleanly to master (include conflict in suspendcontroller.cpp from a371ca87a), so it needs a trivial rebase.
